---
title: "JQI_IndustryExposure_PlotConstruction"
output: html_document
---

```{r, Step 1, include=TRUE}
# =========================================================
# EXPOSURE TO OBJECTIVE JOB QUALITY
# Black - White differences in exposure
# GSS 2000-2024
# =========================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load packages
# ---------------------------------------------------------

library(gssr)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the cumulative GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

data(gss_all)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Select variables needed for the analysis
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi <- gss_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    id,
    racecen1,
    indus10,
    satfin
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Recode personal financial satisfaction
#
# GSS satfin:
# 1 = Satisfied
# 2 = More or less satisfied
# 3 = Not satisfied
#
# Higher values below = greater satisfaction
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi <- gss_jqi %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    financial_satisfaction = dplyr::case_when(
      satfin == 1 ~ 3,
      satfin == 2 ~ 2,
      satfin == 3 ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Construct the common BLS industry classification
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi <- gss_jqi %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(indus10)
    ),
    
    industry_common = dplyr::case_when(
      
      indus10_num == 770 ~ "Construction",
      
      indus10_num >= 1070 &
        indus10_num <= 3990 ~ "Manufacturing",
      
      indus10_num >= 4070 &
        indus10_num <= 4590 ~ "Wholesale trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 4670 &
        indus10_num <= 5790 ~ "Retail trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 6070 &
        indus10_num <= 6390 ~ "Transportation and warehousing",
      
      indus10_num >= 6470 &
        indus10_num <= 6780 ~ "Information",
      
      indus10_num >= 6870 &
        indus10_num <= 6990 ~ "Finance and insurance",
      
      indus10_num >= 7070 &
        indus10_num <= 7190 ~ "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      
      indus10_num >= 7270 &
        indus10_num <= 7490 ~ "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7570 &
        indus10_num <= 7790 ~ "Administrative and support and waste management",
      
      indus10_num >= 7860 &
        indus10_num <= 7890 ~ "Educational services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7970 &
        indus10_num <= 8470 ~ "Health care and social assistance",
      
      indus10_num >= 8560 &
        indus10_num <= 8690 ~ "Leisure and hospitality",
      
      indus10_num >= 8770 &
        indus10_num <= 9290 ~ "Other services",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Load underlying job-quality measures
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_primary <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Construct the three JQI components
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_for_gss <- job_quality_primary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # Compensation
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_premium)
    ),
    
    z_wage_cost = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_cost_per_hour)
    ),
    
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_wage_cost
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Benefits
    z_benefits = as.numeric(
      scale(benefits_nonrequired)
    ),
    
    benefits = z_benefits,
    
    # Earnings stability
    # Higher values = greater stability
    z_earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    ),
    
    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    industry_common,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Merge job quality onto GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi <- gss_jqi %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    job_quality_for_gss,
    by = c(
      "year",
      "industry_common"
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Create the analytic sample
#
# This reproduces the personal-financial-satisfaction
# exposure sample used for the earlier race comparison.
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_exposure <- gss_jqi %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    racecen1 %in% c(1, 2),
    !is.na(financial_satisfaction),
    !is.na(compensation),
    !is.na(benefits),
    !is.na(earnings_stability)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    race_group = dplyr::case_when(
      racecen1 == 1 ~ "White",
      racecen1 == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Check sample sizes
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_exposure %>%
  dplyr::count(race_group)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Calculate White and Black means
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_means <- gss_exposure %>%
  dplyr::group_by(race_group) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    compensation = mean(
      compensation,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    benefits = mean(
      benefits,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    earnings_stability = mean(
      earnings_stability,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Calculate Black - White differences
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_gaps <- exposure_means %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      compensation,
      benefits,
      earnings_stability
    ),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "mean"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = race_group,
    values_from = mean
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    black_white_difference = Black - White
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Inspect the values
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_gaps %>%
  dplyr::select(
    component,
    White,
    Black,
    black_white_difference
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Prepare labels for plotting
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_plot_data <- exposure_gaps %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = dplyr::recode(
      component,
      compensation = "Compensation",
      benefits = "Benefits",
      earnings_stability = "Earnings stability"
    ),
    
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c(
        "Compensation",
        "Benefits",
        "Earnings stability"
      )
    ),
    
    label = sprintf(
      "%+.3f",
      black_white_difference
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Create the plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_plot <- ggplot(
  exposure_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = component,
    y = black_white_difference
  )
) +
  
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  
  geom_col(
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = label
    ),
    vjust = ifelse(
      exposure_plot_data$black_white_difference >= 0,
      -0.5,
      1.5
    ),
    size = 5
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Black − White difference (SD)",
    title = "Exposure to Objective Job Quality"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 16
  ) +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "plain"
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 14
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Display
# ---------------------------------------------------------

exposure_plot


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Save
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "exposure_objective_job_quality_race.png"
  ),
  exposure_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```
